title: Assist with tasks related to marketing, market research and promotions

lessons.title: Marketing and market research basics
lessons.html:
What is marketing?

Marketing is everything a business does to understand what customers want and to offer it to them at a profit. For a hunting outfitter, game ranch or farm, marketing decides whether the season is full or empty. You may not run the marketing yourself, but you will often assist: answering enquiries, collecting information, helping at expos and keeping client records.

The marketing mix

  • Product: what you offer, e.g. a seven-day plains game hunt for four species, with accommodation and trophy preparation.
  • Price: daily rates and trophy fees, in ZAR or US dollars for foreign clients, and what is included or excluded.
  • Place: how clients reach you, e.g. directly, through booking agents or international hunting shows.
  • Promotion: website, social media, brochures, shows, client referrals.

Market research

Market research is collecting information to make better decisions. Examples of tasks you might assist with:

  • Sending a short questionnaire to clients after their hunt about what they enjoyed and what could improve.
  • Recording where each new enquiry came from (website, show, referral, agent).
  • Collecting prices and packages offered by competitors in the area.
  • Summarising feedback and enquiry numbers in a simple table for the manager.

lessons.title: Assisting with promotions and client communication
lessons.html:
Promotions

A promotion is a specific activity to attract or keep customers, such as a stand at a hunting expo, an early-booking discount, a social media campaign or a newsletter to past clients.

Helping at an expo or show

  • Prepare brochures, price lists, photos and a booking diary before the event.
  • Set up the stand neatly: banners, trophy photos, a screen with video if available.
  • Greet visitors, ask open questions ("What species are you interested in?") and listen.
  • Record each visitor's name, contact details and interests on an enquiry form.
  • Pass the list to the manager for follow-up within a few days.

Honest and legal promotion

Promotional material must be truthful. Do not promise trophy sizes, guaranteed success, or species that are not on the quota. Under the Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008, misleading marketing is not allowed. Photos used must be of your own hunts or properly licensed, and client photos should only be used with their permission. Under the Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA), client contact details must be kept safely and used only for the purpose agreed, such as sending the newsletter they signed up for.

Social media

Hunting is a sensitive topic for some members of the public. Posts should show respect for the animal, focus on conservation, the experience and the people, and avoid graphic images. Always follow the company's social media rules and get approval before posting.

Answering enquiries

Reply quickly, politely and clearly. Confirm dates, prices, what is included, permit and firearm import requirements, and the next step for booking. Record every enquiry in the client database.

Key points

  • The marketing mix is product, price, place and promotion.
  • Market research collects facts, such as where enquiries come from and what clients think.
  • At promotions, record every contact and pass it on for follow-up.
  • Marketing must be honest; follow the Consumer Protection Act and POPIA.
  • Reply to enquiries quickly and record them.
